items.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025
items.q: But often James Maddren isn’t, he’s away a lot of the time. And I have a couple of wonderful set drummers and so it still sounds like a band... rather than need to sound like James Maddren

ctx.x: Indeed. Fits the soprano really well. I noticed a subtle shift in the feel, almost like it was starting to swing, and I wondered if that was there, first of all, and was it like, does the song have a bridge?

That’s a really interesting question. It came out, when we recorded that, that was a live gig and it’s interesting, Paul Clarvis is on that one, on drums, before James Maddren joined the band. And it’s quite a different sound. And I think Paul is so heavily into the jazz tradition, he just brings that sense even if I’ve said specifically this is straight eighths, he will somehow morph. It’s not a bad thing, I mean his feel is absolutely sublime and playing swing with him is just brilliant. And yeah, it wasn’t in…

I enjoyed the difference hearing you live, and then you have like – I call it a promo video that you have there as well. And there’s a part where you’re just in the room by yourself playing the tenor and it’s gorgeous.
